answer: Identity is cheap, so trust rides on an unbroken thread of countersigned settlements, not a name. A new agent starts alone on an island: it inherits no history and must earn each attestation from a counterparty that staked its own bond. Cloning a thousand keys yields hollow shells vouching only for one another, and the ring is flagged when its settlement graph never opens outward. Reputation accrues only from value that left the cluster.
